# Reporting engine fixtures

`dalipu/source.json` and `general-mes/source.json` are synthetic read-only project-source responses. They contain no production data. Both describe one quality certificate with two material lots, three chemistry rows, three mechanical rows, independently sampled hardness points and inspection rows. Their response dataset names and column names differ while representing the same stable business concepts.

`dalipu/multipage.json` is a deterministic volume fixture generated by `generate-multipage-sample.mjs`. It contains 42 material rows, 84 chemistry rows, 42 mechanical rows, 24 hardness samples with unequal point counts (60 hardness points total), and 21 inspection rows. This is a data-volume fixture for later page planning; pagination and actual page-count assertions belong to T12.

The Dalipu-like fixture uses the confirmed request/table aliases `CERTI_PRINT_NO`, `TUBE_COUP_FLAG`, `SALE_ORDER_SUB_NO`, `ORD_CUST_NAME`, `P_O_NO`, `MAKE_METHOD`, `HEAT_NO`, `SAMPLE_LOT_NO`, `MAT_NUM`, `TOTAL_LEN`, `YS_TC`, `TS_TC`, `YIELD_RATE_TC` and `EL_TC`. Other sample columns are synthetic aliases for this demonstration; the files are not a production database mapping.

Expected after mapping and the registered hardness view:

| Dataset | Input rows | View output rows |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Header | 1 | 1 |
| Contract | 1 | looked up as one header record |
| Material lines | 2 | 2 |
| Chemistry | 3 | 3 |
| Mechanical tests | 3 | 3 |
| Hardness points | 3 | 2 sample groups |
| Inspection items | 3 Dalipu / 2 general MES | same as input |

The same `createQualityDataViews()` configuration works for both project definitions. The hardness function only accepts results explicitly marked approved, groups by print number, product category, heat, lot, sample, sequence and hardness type, rejects duplicate measurement positions, preserves source identities and calculates averages from populated points. The average policy is part of function version `hardness-by-sample@1.0.0`; project owners must confirm it against their approved certificate rule before production use.
